name: Blume Ventures
identity_check: Blume Ventures at blume.vc: an early-stage Indian venture firm founded in 2010 by Karthik Reddy and Sanjay Nath. Manager entities named on its Contact/About pages are Blume Venture Advisors Private Limited and Blume Venture Investment Manager LLP (registered office Byculla East, Mumbai; branch in GIFT City, Gandhinagar); offices in Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi, GIFT City and San Francisco. Confirmed by domain, the firm's own About, Funds and team pages, and fund-close press (Inc42, Entrackr, Entrepreneur India) naming the same partners and funds. Its LinkedIn company page is blume-venture-advisors. Not any other company that uses the name Blume. The blume.vc homepage (with its FAQ) returned HTTP 403 throughout; subpages were readable.

thesis_text.value: Indian early-stage VC backing tech-led startups mainly at seed and pre-Series A, sometimes leading Series A. Fund V writes $1.5–5M first cheques with deep reserves, targeting 30–35 companies across consumer, fintech, health tech and deep tech; recent deals include B2B AI agents, electronics and toy ODMs and voice AI. A San Francisco-based co-founder covers cross-border AI and SaaS.

Co-founder Sanjay Nath is based in San Francisco and focuses on cross-border AI and SaaS; 2026 Perspectives says Blume set up a Bay Area presence.
Fund V: first close USD 175M (Oct 2025), target USD 250-275M final close 'by early 2026'; no final close found (web search budget ran out mid-task). size_original left null as first close only.

Funds page mentions 'a secondary fund, multiple opportunity funds, and special purpose vehicles' without names, sizes or dates. An Outlook Startup article titled 'Blume Ventures raises Rs 200 crore for its opportunity fund' was unreachable (connection refused). No 'Blume Founders Fund' found.
Fund I and Fund II close dates not stated (only investing periods 2011-14 and 2015-17). Fund III close month comes from the DealStreetAsia headline date (19 Feb 2020); article body paywalled.
Funds page still says Blume is 'presently investing out of Fund IV' although Fund V has 12 companies; page appears stale.
No pitch form: the Contact page lists a pitch email (not recorded) and asks founders to read the homepage FAQ first.
